grades.quote: RISC-V base ISAs have either little-endian or big-endian memory systems, with the privileged architecture further defining bi-endian operation. Instructions are stored in memory as a sequence of 16-bit little-endian parcels, regardless of memory system endianness.
grades.reason: Directly states RISC-V byte-order rules: memory systems may be little- or big-endian (bi-endian in the privileged architecture), while instructions are always stored as 16-bit little-endian parcels. It covers only the RISC-V side of the comparison and says nothing about LoongArch.
Covers I/O and memory ordering (fences, MMIO) in RVWMO. This is about access ordering, not byte order or endianness.
Describes the cache-block zero instruction (cbo.zero). It does not mention byte order or endianness.
Lists LoongArch integer data type sizes and says they use two's complement encoding. It does not state the byte order (endianness) of memory accesses.
